Titan Quest is a dungeon crawler action RPG comparable to Diablo. It is set in ancient Greek, Egypt and China with all of it’s mythological monsters and lots of loot. I have played Titan Quest and the expansion The Immortal Throne a lot as a child. I was a bit too late for the Diablo 2 hype and found my fun in this dungeon crawler. So I might be a bit nostalgic.

[b]What I liked[/b]
- Zen-like: These kind of games always get me in a zen-like flow. Most of the game you don’t have to think too much and you just gather up all the valuables and peruse them for anything of use. Occasionally a boss or sometimes even random hero will show up that kills you in 2-3 hits. So you still have to be on your toes.

- Theme: One thing I always liked about Titan Quest is that it really goes all in on its “Ancient world” theme. Some enemies are taken from well known mythical monsters while others are obscure beasts that still feel at home in the environment. It all looks and feels very authentic.

- Mastery system: The choosing of two masteries makes it that you have a lot of different characters you can make. I don’t think I have a single mastery that I do not like. The runemaster also makes a nice addition with the Ragnarok DLC.

- Easter Egg: I played the game a lot but I never noticed this easter egg in the Immortal Throne where you get to fight the developers. I had a lot of fun with the weird properties of these enemies named after the devs. It was a very fitting ending.

[b]What I didn’t like[/b]
- Performance: The game doesn’t seem to run that well at times. It didn’t happen often but I did have moments where I had my frames drop. Which can be quite deadly in this game.

- Attack speed OP: Part of the fun of these kind of games is too try out different loot you find. Unfortunately one stat is just so good in makes the choosing of your equipment mostly trivial. Picking the item with an attack speed or total speed modifier is most of the times the right choose. I think the game would have been more interesting without this modifier.

- Dps meter unreliable: I’m still not sure but what I found on the internet it seems the dps meter that is shown in your inventory is not taken everything in mind. In my experience it also made some weird calculations when comparing items. This is a shame because comparing items is part of the fun in this game but hard to do because of this.

- Casting Time: There seems to be this weird delay before you actually activate a skill. I think it is the modifier called casting time. It makes me feel like the game is unresponsive. When I press a button I expect the skill to be activated. 

- Backtracking: I like to explore every corner of the map and don’t mind backtracking in those cases but when you have to backtrack for a side quest through empty terrain it is quite boring. The Immortal Throne has a annoying one with a Deamon NPC in a camp for example. I would have preferred if they just had a teleporter near all of these locations.  

- Collision problems: During some parts of the game it is noticeable that height difference is not taken into account when shooting a ranged attack at an enemy. I had some cases where arrows get stuck in staircases or slopes. I also had two instances of my character getting stuck in a door that just opened. The only way to get out of it was to teleport to the nearest circle and walk all the way back. 

- Quality of life missing: I wished they had some kind of way to quickly cast a buff on yourself. The fire resistance shield from the earth mastery is annoying to have to keep casting on yourself. One click to activate it and another on your portrait every half a minute or so gets tedious. This could have been 1 click with some kind of toggle. 

- Need more storage: I like to collect. Especially the blue items are cool to collect but your bank space will quickly get full. I was forced to make “mule” characters to save more items. And that is quite a hassle to do. I think it is new that there is now a dedicated relic page which is good but still not enough. I would install a mod for it if it didn’t disable achievements. EDIT: I have been using a program called Titan Quest Vault to fix this problem. It doesn't disable achievements and is easy enough to use.

- Shadowmaw: half way through Greece there is a cave that in the original was not that special. Now however it houses an enemy that has a much higher level then enemies in the rest of the area. I’m pretty sure it killed me in 1 hit the first time I encountered him. There is an achievement attached to him if you kill him before leaving Greece but still I don’t really like the change they made here.

[b]Why others should try it[/b]
If you just want to click away in a dungeon crawler you can do a lot worse then Titan Quest. Another game that recently came out, Grim Dawn, is very similar and also from one of Titan Quest’s creators. I do think Grim Dawn is the better game with more systems and a smoother experience. Of course there is more games like this. For example Diablo 3 for a more triple A experience, Path of Exile for a free to play game that is constantly updated or Torchlight 2 for a more stylized game. These are all good games but if you really like the theme of Titan Quest or have nostalgia like me you might still want to go for this game.

A classic game that still looks and feels great after many years. I run into players frequently who are surprised to learn this game is two decades old. I have played TQ since it first came out and I find myself going back to it time and time again. Unlike many other aging games that get revitalized with a facelift of updated graphics, Titan Quest is getting brand new content -- certainly a testimonial of it's popularity.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
Great graphics
Character creation (ten Masteries for a total of 55 possible character classes).
Updated with new content ([i][b]Ragnarok, Atlantis,[/b][/i] and [i][b]Eternal Embers[/b][/i]).

[h1]Cons[/h1]
A lot of hackers (I mean [i] a lot[/i]). This is best played solo or with a group of friends.

[h1] Mythological World [/h1]

Titan Quest is a classic diablo-like ARPG set in ancient time. Most of the game is set to the ancient Greece where you fight against all kinds of mythological creatures, but there are also parts of the game set in Egypt and Asia, which I would call a weak point of the game. Greece is detailed and the story is rich and I think that is the reason why most of the players I know never finished the basic game or even got farther then the second chapter.  

There are also other things you should consider before playing. Even though the game offers variety of specializations (hunter, assassin etc.), the rate at which you gain or enhance your character and it‘s abilities slows down pretty quickly. In the beginning, the game (Greece) is pretty quick and most enjoyable, but the further you are, your development is slower and the game becomes more boring. Mostly because there is a wide scale of skills which are useless for you because you have to focus on only a few to make them effective. For example, I finished the basic game + the immortal throne at level 37 only with 1 attack ability, 1 conjured minion and a bunch of passive abilities.  

[h1] Summary [/h1]

[b]Pros[/b]

✪ [i]Great interpretation of Greek Mythology [/i] 
✪ [i]Classic ARPG[/i] 
✪ [i]Great Coop[/i] 
✪ [i]Varied skill system[/i] 
✪ [i]Well-arranged UI[/i] 

[b]Cons[/b]

✪ [i]Slow progress [/i] 
✪ [i]Very grindy and repetitive gameplay[/i]
✪ [i]Loot is very random[/i] (e.g. its normal not to find any better equipment for 15 levels)
✪ [i]Slow character progress[/i] 

[b]6/10[/b] 

I can recommend the game for its great setting and good and enjoyable multiplayer. On the other hand in my opinion, there are much better ARPGs out there you should try first.

An old but gold aRPG hack'n'slash game with lots of replayability value. The original game came out in 2006 and its mindblowing how fun it can be to this day. The story is good, the mechanics are good, but might be weird or difficult to adapt to if you play a lot of other aRPGs, but overall I find it easy to adapt to the game. The devs are actively working on the game, showing it love, so its definitely not an abandoned project, which is mindblowing for a game this old. The skill system works well, theres 10 masteries (10 with 1st DLC, without it its 9) from which to choose, you can pick 2 on each character, theres a lot of variety when it comes to what you can do in the game, which works well since the map is always the same and you have 3 difficulties, meaning you'll be playing the same map 3 times to actually finish the game, with each difficulty getting progressively harder of course. Theres 2 DLCs for this game, the 1st one being Ragnarok, which is absolutely great, 10/10 DLC, definitely worth it, recapturing the feel of the old Titan Quest. 2nd DLC is Atlantis, and that one.... while I myself like it, cuz I love the game in general, I cant in good faith recommend that one to someone new coming in to the game. As of writing this review, the DLC is 6 months old, and its half baked at best. FPS drops when killing creatures, visual bugs, not all items are implemented.... If you already love TQ, you most can get atlantis and you most likely wont regret it, as it introduces a lot of new and good ideas to the game, 2 more skills per each mastery, new suffix on items "of the tinkerer" which allows you to enhance items with relics/charms twice, so much goodness for an old TQ fan. However if youre a new player and are just looking for stable and normal gameplay- then i suggest you for now skip out on Atlantis, but definitely get Ragnarok DLC, as it will unlock Rune mastery and throwing weapons, and unlock the whole Nordic area- which will definitely improve your experience! With the atlantis update, even if you dont get the DLC itself- the game has been upgraded to Dx11, making it look really damn good for its time, considering it has been out for about 13 years now! While  nothing special in the graphics department do to its age, the graphics are nothing to scoff at, and Id say they hold up pretty damn well! Oh, and I forgot- The music! The fucking music in this game is better than it has any right to be! The boss battle music is hype, the regular OSTs are beautiful, ESPECIALLY the Atlantis OSTs. This game is definitely worth it, especially on sales when it goes for dirt cheap, Id wholeheartedly recommend this one to any aRPG fan and its 1st DLC, while for the Atlantis DLC Id say hold off until the devs fix some things, then I'd say go for that one as well!
Very fun, from a biased fanboy perspective its a 10/10, while if I were to suspend my feelings of the game Id say its a solid 8.5/10 with its 1st DLC, while with the 2nd DLC Id say a 7/10 (until they fix its issues).

I fully recommend this game. Read on if you want to know why.

The pros:
Although this game was released in 2006 the graphics are still holding up with nowadays games.
But not only the graphics are great even the artstyle is an outstandig masterpiece.
It's not too dark or too colorful.
The game is set in pre-roman ironage mixed up with mythologie.
It's a really well fitiing and unspent setting.
The character progression and skilling is interesting.
The sound ambient and music is well made and catching.
The developer delivered all of the tools the games have been made with, so you can make your own Titan Quest mod or total conversion.

The cons:
The controls feel a bit clumpy. You often get stuck on small clutter on the ground you're barely seeing.
The game doesn't recognize when you're pressing multiple buttons at once for activating skills for example.
This can be the reason why you die rather quickly and thats frustrating.
Sometimes the frames drop at a low rate when special effects like rain or snow are showing.
Even though you can expand your bag the room to hoard stuff is very limited. You need to use third-party-tools like TQVault to expand you stash.
This also applies to the attributes like strength, dexterity, intelligence etc. You need to use third-party-tools to reset them.
The devs have added some lategame contenct but it's not enough to keep the players busy imo.

All in all it's a great game that you should play.
